hypotheses.justification: Both hU and hV can be deleted, even simultaneously. Replace each chart's frame functor by a componentwise version: on the basepoint's path component use chosen arrows and φU or φV; on every other component send all arrows to 1. Choose the arrows on the intersection using intersectionArrow, which requires only hI. These functors agree on the intersection by hcompat, so FundamentalGroupoid.descOfIsOpenCover and inclusion_comp_descOfIsOpenCover give the required homomorphism. For uniqueness, subdivide any based loop into chart-contained pieces, as in morphismProperty_of_isOpenCover, and merge consecutive pieces in the same chart. All remaining endpoints lie in the intersection. Closing each piece using intersection paths expresses the loop as a product of images of based chart loops; Path.Homotopic.concat_subpath justifies the subdivision equality. Thus the restrictions determine the homomorphism. The point p guarantees a nonempty intersection; additional path components and trivial groups cause no exceptions.

The same componentwise-frame construction and loop-subdivision argument described for hU works symmetrically without hV. Only the intersection needs paths from p to transition points. Components of V not containing p receive the trivial functor and do not affect based loops. The point p excludes an empty intersection, and the construction also works for trivial target groups. Both hU and hV may be deleted simultaneously.
